mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points above 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5% and 3mo change > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) signal robust consumer demand expansion, boosting corporate revenue visibility and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS increase month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 2.5% year-over-year triggers expectations of Federal Reserve tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) declining below 100 (2017=100) signals manufacturing sector contraction, reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: Rising year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary economic momentum, stimulating corporate revenue growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days through improved earnings outlook.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when year-over-year CPIAUCSL growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous nonfarm payroll growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate decline (UNRATE) signal strengthening labor market conditions, increasing consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth below 1.0% annualized (GDPC1) signals economic contraction, reducing corporate earnings expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 growth rate < 1.0% annualized.
